item.text: {"text":"HSTU’s official 2024 MovieLens configuration uses sampled softmax with 128 negatives, L2-normalized item/user embeddings and temperature 0.05—a practical objective reference, not evidence of optimal Amazon settings. [Official configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin). Research supports investigating misleadingly easy training negatives: Scalable Cross-Entropy (2024) targets informative catalog items through approximate maximum-inner-product search; Correcting LogQ (2025) addresses sampling bias, emphasizing that the positive target is always present rather than sampled. Neither establishes gains for HSTU on these four categories. [SCE paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721), [LogQ paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331).\n\nPractical hypothesis: retain one HSTU per category and compare larger uniform-negative sampled softmax against a gradual mixture of uniform and model-mined, moderately hard negatives. Avoid automatically selecting only the highest-scoring items: unobserved interactions can be false negatives, making aggressive mining distort learning. Exclude known training positives and target collisions; never consult held-out interactions for filtering. [Negative-sampling survey, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1145/3793855). These are proposed experiments, not measured improvements. Select using the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10, with Electronics reported separately; low training loss or large sampled margins alone cannot establish ranking quality. Keep normalization, temperature and negative count explicit in comparisons, preserve the HSTU backbone and predictor consistency, and retain exactly one trained checkpoint per category."}
